localContext: Evanston’s specific climate and housing stock affect garage door tracks. Many homes, especially in South Evanston and the West Village, feature century-old Victorians and brick homes with original detached garages on rear alleys. These older structures often have garage doors and tracks exposed to decades of weather. Lake-effect snow, strong winds, and moisture off Lake Michigan corrode garage door hardware. Salt air, prevalent in first-ring suburbs like Evanston, speeds up rust on hinges, rollers, and even track surfaces. This rust and corrosion cause rollers to bind or tracks to misalign. Older garages on rear alleys are also susceptible to vehicle impact. A small bump can bend a track section. We understand these local challenges. We provide track repair solutions suited for Evanston’s unique environment and historic garage door systems.

problemSigns.detail: Your garage door struggles to move past a specific point. It might stop completely or operate unevenly.

problemSigns.detail: A separation here indicates loose track brackets or a bent track section pulling away from the wall.
